facts.fact: A goat path leaves the cart road left of a lightning-split boulder at the Monkey Pass gorge below the last pass village, climbs the scree and the shoulder, and drops through thorn past an old well to the lower waystation. Neela knows it without a map and cannot say how.
facts.why: needed because the outline has her lead them round the rockfall by a path she knows (clue C22 / reader question).

facts.fact: The lower waystation is a low laterite house with a well, a carters' shed and a trodden yard; it stands empty between seasons.
facts.why: needed because the beat sends them to inspect the lower waystation.

facts.fact: Six men rested at the waystation two nights ago and left north before dawn on foot; Neela reads their boots as a trained soldier's heel, a rider's wear and new coast-stitched soles, so they were fed and brought most of the way rather than walking from the sea.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Devan read the tracks and Neela the boot-wear; kept as a small clue with no named culprit.

facts.fact: Kesu is a one-eyed grandfather in one of the pass villages.
facts.why: a villager name for Neela's habit of learning names.

facts.fact: Neela counts thirty-two nights left on the morning of chapter 9, the day after the writ arrives.
facts.why: continues the night count from chapters 4, 6 and 7.
